name: Peapods Finance (Ethereum): Yoink completes the attacker's pair-2 exploit after three failed attempts
headline_text: After the attacker's pair-1 exploit (+78.19 ETH) and three reverted pair-2 attempts, Yoink replayed the same 42-call recipe one block later and took 174,258 USDC with an 11.49 ETH bribe; it returned 126,892 USDC (90% after cost). No pending attacker tx is shown.
verdict_reason: Press (Phalcon/BlockSec, Quadriga) says the attacker's 'second attempt' was front-run by Yoink. On chain, the attacker ran the exploit on pair 1 (WETH market) at block 22873986 idx 4 and netted 78.186 ETH, then tried pair 2 (USDC market 0xca1154bb) in three consecutive blocks 22874007/08/09. Each pair-2 leg reverted inside the attacker's try/catch (outer tx status 1, no profit). Yoink's tx0 (22874010 idx 0, 12 s after the last attempt) has the same state-changing call sequence as all three attempts (42 of 42 calls, identical Morpho loan of 10,000,000 USDC, identical UniV3 swap and Curve exchange sizes) and its borrowAsset passed, taking 174,258.31 USDC. So Yoink adapted a landed, failing attacker tx and completed it. It did not pre-empt a pending attacker tx that we can show: the attacker's earlier attempts had already landed, the attacker's calldata run on the pre-Yoink state still reverts (debug_traceCall), and neither side's txs are in the public mempool archive. Yoink's tx did exhaust the opportunity (the attacker's later attempts 22874015/16 stop at 'zero token'). Per the publication policy (confirmed-onchain needs the bot to be first or to pre-empt a pending tx) this is a post-failure replay, not a headline win.
protocol_loss_note: Press/CertiK figure (~$200k, ~78 ETH) matches the attacker's pair-1 take (78.186 ETH). Yoink's pair-2 take (174,258.31 USDC) is additional: the pair-2 funding vault 0x3717e340 fell from 463,970.31 to 115,704.36 USDC at block 22874010.

limits: Yoink's trigger is unknown: both sides used private flow (no tx in mempool-dumpster). The first large bid (4.91 ETH, beaverbuild, -5.9 s into slot 12095680) appears 6.1 s after the attacker's block 22874009 was sealed; that bounds, but does not prove, Yoink reacting to an on-chain attempt.
Whether the attacker had a tx pending for block 22874010 is unknown. The attacker sent one tx per block in bursts (22873986-88, 22874007-09, 22874015-16); none is included at 22874010.
Why the attacker's pair-2 borrowAsset reverts while Yoink's passes is not determined (attacker contract unverified; revert error 0xed27783c(uint256) not decoded).
Counterfactual 'would the attacker have succeeded without Yoink' is bounded by one simulation on the pre-Yoink state (reverts); later blocks cannot be simulated without Yoink's tx.
Yoink's stated cost (11.95248 ETH) differs from the measured coinbase total (11.98767 ETH) by 0.035 ETH; not reconciled.
ETH-equivalents of USDC use the vault's own swap proceeds, not a price oracle.

harmonized.verdict_reason: Press (Phalcon/BlockSec via Quadriga, Peapods' thank-you message) says Yoink front-ran the attacker's second attempt. On chain the attacker (EOA 0x277da2d1) succeeded on pair 1 at block 22873986 idx 4 (+78.19 ETH), then tried the USDC pair 0xca1154bb in blocks 22874007/08/09 (txs 0xdc774417, 0x505db202, 0xa03582cc); each pair-2 leg reverted inside the attacker's try/catch. Yoink's tx 0xff8e9226 (block 22874010 idx 0, 12 s after the last attempt) has the same 42 state-changing calls (role-normalised similarity 1.0, same 10M USDC Morpho loan, same swap sizes) and its borrow passed, taking 174,258.31 USDC (11.4944 ETH to coinbase, no builder refund). No attacker tx is shown pending: the attempts had already landed, the attacker's calldata on the pre-Yoink state still reverts (debug_traceCall), and none of either side's txs is in the mempool archive. Yoink adapted and completed a failed, already-mined attack; it did not pre-empt anything we can show. Yoink returned 126,891.81 USDC (90% after recouping 33,267 USDC for its stated 11.95 ETH bribe).
